parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the dimensions of a boiling tube. The apparatus has been set up for you. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1.

ms.label: 1(a)
ms.text:
sensible value for h0
and precaution for reading water level e.g.:
view scale perpendicularly /
rule close to boiling tube /
use of set square

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Using the dropping pipette, and measuring cylinder if necessary, add a further volume of water V = 5.0 cm 3 to the water already in the boiling tube. Measure, and record in Table 1.1, the new height h of the water level from the bench. Repeat this procedure, adding 5.0 cm 3 of water each time so that the total volume of water added V = 10.0 cm 3 , 15.0 cm 3 , 20.0 cm 3 and 25.0 cm 3 . Table 1.1 V / cm 3 h / cm H / cm 5.0 10.0 15.0 20.0 25.0 [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) For each value of V , calculate, and record in Table 1.1, the increase in height H of the water in the boiling tube. Use your value of h 0 from (a) , the values of h in Table 1.1 and the equation H = ( h – h 0 ). [1]

ms.label: 1(c)
ms.text: H calculations correct and all with consistent decimal places

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Plot a graph of V / cm 3 ( y -axis) against H / cm ( x -axis). [4]

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
graph:
•
axes labelled with quantity and unit
•
appropriate scales (occupying at least ½ grid)
•
plots all correct to ½ small square and precise plots
•
well-judged line and thin line

parts.label: i
parts.text: (e) (i) Determine the gradient of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. gradient = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 1(e)(i)
ms.text: G present and triangle method shown on graph grid

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate D , the inside diameter of the boiling tube. Use the equation D = 4 G π , where G is numerically equivalent to the gradient in (e)(i) . D = ................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 1(e)(ii)
ms.text: D in range 2.0 cm to 3.0 cm

ms.label: 1(f)
ms.text: inside diameter near base not uniform / owtte

ms.label: 1(g)
ms.text:
valid critical comment e.g.:
water volumes small – large (%) uncertainty
test-tube diameter small – large (%) uncertainty in answer
owtte
height changes small so unreliable
